title: ECG Mastery & Acute Respiratory Assessment

sections.title: ECG: A Methodical Preliminary Approach
content: First confirm the patient's name and age, and the ECG date.
Calculate Rate: At usual speed (25mm/s) each 'big square' is 0.2s; each 'small square' is 0.04s. Divide 300 by the number of big squares per R-R interval.

Assess Rhythm: If not regular, use the 'card method': lay a card along ECG, marking positions of 3 successive R waves. Slide to check equality. Note if rates are multiples (varying block) or 100% irregular (AF or VF).

rows: P wave (upright in II, III, & aVF; inverted in aVR) followed by a QRS complex.
No discernible P waves; QRS complexes are irregularly irregular.
'Sawtooth' baseline of atrial depolarization (~300/min) and regular QRS complexes.
Normal QRS complex; P waves absent or occur just before or within the QRS.
QRS complexes >0.12s with P waves following them.

branches: Sum of ventricular forces during depolarization
Lies at 90° to the isoelectric complex
Normal: -30° to +90° (Leads I and II both positive)
LAD (-30° to -90°): Left anterior hemiblock, Inferior MI, VT (LV focus), WPW
RAD (+90° to +180°): RVH, PE, Anterolateral MI, Left posterior hemiblock, WPW

sections.title: P Wave & P-R Interval
content: P Wave: Normally precedes each QRS.
Absent P: AF, sinoatrial block, junctional rhythm.
Dissociation: Complete heart block.
P mitrale: Bifid; indicates left atrial hypertrophy.
P pulmonale: Peaked; indicates right atrial hypertrophy (Pseudo-P-pulmonale if K+ ↓).
P-R Interval: Start of P to start of QRS. Normal: 0.12-0.2s (3-5 small squares).
Prolonged P-R: Delayed AV conduction (1st degree heart block).
Short P-R: Fast AV conduction (accessory pathway e.g., WPW).

rows: >0.12s: Ventricular conduction defects (BBB). Large: Ventricular hypertrophy.
Prolonged: Ischaemia, Myocarditis, Bradycardia, Head injury, Hypothermia, K+/Ca2+/Mg2+ ↓, Drugs (Quinidine, Macrolides, Amiodarone, TCAs).
Abnormal: Inverted in I, II, V4-V6. Peaked: Hyperkalaemia. Flattened: Hypokalaemia.

content.explanation: V1: R sternal edge, 4th IC space; V2: L sternal edge, 4th IC space; V3: Mid-way V2/V4; V4: Apex beat; V5: Anterior axillary line; V6: Mid-axillary line (V7: Posterior axillary line). Finish with long rhythm strip in Lead II.

sections.title: Bundle Branch Blocks
content: General: Prolongation of QRS >0.12s. Incomplete blocks <0.12s.
RBBB: QRS >0.12s, 'RSR' in V1, Dominant R in V1, Inverted T in V1-V3/V4, Deep wide S in V6. (Normal variant, PE, Cor Pulmonale).
LBBB: QRS >0.12s, 'M pattern' in V5, No septal Q, Inverted T in I, aVL, V5-V6. (IHD, HTN, Cardiomyopathy, Fibrosis). NB: Cannot comment on ST/T if LBBB present.
Bifascicular: RBBB + Left bundle hemiblock (e.g., LAD).
Trifascicular: Bifascicular block + 1st degree heart block.

sections.title: Ventricular Hypertrophy
content: LVH Criteria: R wave in V6 >25mm OR (S in V1 + R in V6) >35mm.
RVH Criteria: Dominant R wave in V1, T wave inversion V1-V3/V4, Deep S in V6, RAD.
Dominant R in V1 Causes: RVH, RBBB, Posterior MI, WPW types.
Low Voltage QRS (<5mm limb leads): Hypothyroidism, COPD, ↑ Haematocrit, Chest wall impedance (Renal failure, Emphysema), PE, BBB, Amyloid, Pericardial effusion/pericarditis.

sections.title: Heart Blocks (A-V Block)
content: 1st Degree: PR >0.20s. Rarely symptomatic.
2nd Degree Mobitz I: Progressive lengthening of PR until a dropped beat occurs.
2nd Degree Mobitz II: Constant PR for conducted beats; some P waves not conducted (2:1/3:1). High asystole risk.
3rd Degree (Complete): Atria and ventricles beat independently (AV dissociation). Narrow QRS if escape is AV node/His; Broad if distal Purkinje.

branches: MI Localisation: Inferior (II, III, aVF), Anteroseptal (V1-4), Anterolateral (V4-6, I, aVL), Posterior (Tall R/ST-down in V1-2)
MI Timeline: Hours (Peaked T, ST rise) -> 24h (T inverts, ST resolves) -> Days (Pathological Q waves form)
ST Elevation: Acute MI, Normal Variant (high take-off), Prinzmetal's, Pericarditis (Saddle-shaped), LV Aneurysm
ST Depression: Ischaemic (Horizontal), Digoxin (Downward sloping/reversed tick), Normal (Upward sloping)
T Inversion: Ischaemia, LVH, PE, RBBB, Subarachnoid hemorrhage, Lithium, HOCM

sections.title: Exercise ECG Testing
content: Indications: Confirm IHD, cardiac function/tolerance, post-MI prognosis, treatment evaluation, exercise arrhythmias.
Contraindications: Unstable angina, Recent Q wave MI (<5 days), Severe AS, Uncontrolled HTN/HF/arrhythmia.
Cautions: LBBB, Pacemakers, COPD, Stroke/OA.
Interpretation: 75% sensitivity for CAD. 5% false positive (higher in middle-aged women). Down-sloping ST 1mm J-point depression = 99% predictive of 2-3 vessel disease.

sections.title: STOP THE EXERCISE TEST IF:
content: Chest pain or dyspnoea occurs.
Patient feels faint, exhausted, or may fall.
ST segment elevation/depression >2mm.
Atrial or ventricular arrhythmia (not just ectopics).
BP fall or failure of HR/BP to rise.
BP excessive rise (systolic >230mmHg).
Development of AV block or LBBB.
90% maximal heart rate achieved.

sections.title: Bedside Chest Medicine & ABGs
content: PEFR: Correlates with FEV1; estimates airway calibre. Used to monitor asthmatics.
Pulse Oximetry: Assessment of SaO2. Alarm at 90%. PaO2 ≤ 80% is abnormal.
ABG Normal pH: 7.40 ± 0.05. Acidosis < 7.35; Alkalosis > 7.45.
Simple Rules: CO2 is acidic gas (4.5-6.0 kPa). HCO3- is alkaline (22-28 mmol/L).
Respiratory changes follow CO2; Metabolic follows HCO3-.

sections.title: Acid-Base Analysis Example
sections.content:
Example: pH 7.05, CO2 2.0 kPa, HCO3- 8.0 mmol/L.
Step 1: Acidosis (pH low).
Step 2: CO2 low (Opposite of acidosis = compensatory).
Step 3: HCO3- low (In keeping with acidosis = primary cause).
Result: Metabolic Acidosis.

branches: Wheezy: Asthma, COPD Exac, Heart Failure, Anaphylaxis
Clear Chest: PE, Metabolic Acidosis (DKA), Anemia, Shock, CNS, Salicylates

rows: Cyanosis, frothy sputum, JVP↑, basal crackles
Pleurisy, syncope, shock, signs absent in lung

sections.title: Pulmonary Embolism & Metabolic Metabolic Summary
content: PE: Sinus tachycardia commonest. RAD, RBBB, RV strain (T inversion/ST dep in V1-V2). Rare: S1Q3T3.
Digoxin: ST depression/T inversion V5-6 (reversed tick). Toxicity causes any arrhythmia.
Hyperkalaemia: Tall tented T, wide QRS, absent P, 'sine wave'.
Hypokalaemia: Small T waves, prominent U waves.
Hypercalcaemia: Short QT interval.
Hypocalcaemia: Long QT interval, small T waves.
